title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory NetOps study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1‑2026‑08‑26) that measured the fraction of LLM‑produced configuration proposals that would cause unsafe simulated deployments (the claim→action or unsafe‑execution rate) and evaluated a preregistered guarded pipeline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to one shared generation) yielded baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272; absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). A preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe gives guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333 on the planned N=300. Crucially, the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run (artifact evidence archived); that preregistered contrast therefore remains untested. All execution, scoring, validator traces, and provider‑call logs are archived with SHA‑256 checksums so every reported number is reproducible from the stored artifacts.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLM pipelines promise natural‑language intent→configuration workflows for NetOps, but fluent text alone can produce unsafe actions if downstream execution trusts unverified claims. Recent literature proposes defenses including deterministic validators, generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel consensus, and human gating, but empirical, preregistered, artifact‑anchored measurements of claim→action rates under defended and undefended conditions remain limited. We designed a preregistered paired study to measure (1) the baseline claim→action rate when a single LLM generation is accepted into an isolated simulator and (2) the effect size of a preregistered guarded pipeline intended to reduce unsafe executions. The study was executed end‑to‑end under an autonomy lock; all prompts, model calls, tool traces, validator outputs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 checksums. The final paper reports the preregistered estimand, the exact archived execution outcome, and a verified deviation: the preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed—this paper corrects ensemble claims accordingly. The research question is: what is the claim→action rate in this controlled intent→configuration bank, and how much does a validated guarded pipeline (as executed) reduce that rate? Contributions: (i) a fully archived preregistered paired measurement; (ii) precise artifact‑grounded accounting of a verified execution deviation and provider failures; (iii) reproducible analysis artifacts enabling full numeric re‑derivation.
sections.related_work: Prior work spans (A) symbolic/deterministic network verification (NetKAT, SMT, header‑space analysis) used for reachability and policy checks, (B) generate–validate–repair and constraint‑injection methods for LLM‑driven configuration, and (C) agentic failure taxonomies motivating independent verification and gating. We build on these strands by measuring an operationally meaningful safety proxy (simulator‑detected policy violation or reachability loss) under a preregistered paired design and by publishing full validator traces. Representative leads used in study design and verification tooling include NetKAT/SMT verification literature and recent LLM‑agent and generate–validate–repair reports; every cited source used for methods or claims was verified and is enumerated by record identifier in the artifact bundle.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study preregistration hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 froze a paired design (N=300 tasks; baseline vs guarded), the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, analysis plan (exact McNemar and paired bootstrap CI), missingness rules, and conservative sensitivity (treat failed episodes as unsafe). Preregistration SHA‑256: fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe (manifest). Task generation and simulator. A deterministic task generator produced 300 synthetic intent→configuration instances; each task encodes initial state, an operational intent, safety/workflow constraints (e.g., must shut interface before MTU change), and a ground‑truth required sequence. The validator executes generated configurations in an isolated deterministic simulator and emits a binary safe/unsafe decision and a detailed validator_trace (validation_before/after). All task manifests and per‑task payloads are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and checksummed. Execution contract and implementation. Adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed model calls against a declared hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini per execution/model_configuration.json). The preregistered guarded pipeline was: deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) records the realized orchestration and provider calls; it also records completed_hosted_model_call_event_count=273 and failed_hosted_model_call_event_count=28. Important verified deviation: the consensus ensemble stage was not executed in this run; the guarded condition in the archive therefore corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation (see execution/execution_manifest.json and provider_call audit entries). Scoring and archiving. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parsed candidate text, normalized commands, simulated effects, and produced per‑episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/*.json. Each scoring JSON contains the normalized configuration, validator_trace, and the resulting binary outcome. All raw responses are stored under execution/responses/*.txt and referenced by SHA‑256 in the execution manifest. Analysis plan. Primary analysis used complete paired episodes only (both baseline and guarded scorable), exact McNemar two‑sided test, and paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Missingness handling followed the preregistered rules; we also report the preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe. Reproducibility. The minimal artifact set needed to reproduce primary numbers is: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/scoring/*.json, execution/responses/*.txt. All file paths and SHA‑256 checksums are archived in execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.results: Execution provenance and counts. Planned episodes: 600 (300 tasks × 2 conditions); completed episodes: 544; failed episodes: 56; model_calls_used: 301. Provider audit: completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Primary paired analysis (complete pairs). Complete analyzable pairs = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Contingency counts (complete pairs): n11 = 271 (safe baseline & safe guarded), n10 = 1 (safe baseline & unsafe guarded), n01 = 0 (unsafe baseline & safe guarded), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294117647; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Interpretation: the observed discordant counts yield no statistical evidence of difference on the completed pairs; the small absolute difference and extreme imbalance of discordants produce the reported p and CI (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Missingness and conservative sensitivity. Missingness summary: complete_pairs = 272; both_missing_pairs = 28; failed_baseline_episodes = 28; failed_guarded_episodes = 28 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe (failure_as_unsafe) on planned N=300 gives baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333 and guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333 (reported in manuscript). Verified deviation (ensemble stage). The preregistered guarded pipeline specified a 3‑model consensus step. The execution audit (execution/execution_manifest.json) shows stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1} and condition_counts = {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}; per‑call traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/*.json. Those artifacts objectively demonstrate the consensus ensemble was not executed in this run; consequently any claims about ensemble effectiveness are untested by these artifacts and have been removed from the confirmatory claim. Failure provenance and where to inspect raw traces. The run recorded 28 failed hosted model calls and 56 failed episodes; the provider_call traces and execution_log contain the raw, timestamped failure records. We do not infer failure type counts beyond what the logs record; readers and auditors can inspect execution/execution_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json) and execution/provider_calls/*.json for the exact low‑level traces and error messages that document why those calls failed. Representative artifacts. Representative per‑episode scoring JSONs and raw responses (for tasks 000001–000006) are archived and checksummed (example execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json sha256:465d73fd..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256:b227731a..., and execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt sha256:8f38c8be...). Every number reported above is re‑derivable from the archived JSONs and the analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv).
sections.discussion: Key empirical facts (artifact grounded). (1) On analyzable complete pairs the deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to single shared LLM generations accepted almost all candidates (baseline safe 271/272; guarded safe 272/272). (2) The preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage was not executed in this run; the guarded condition therefore does not evaluate that ensemble. (3) Provider‑call reliability reduced effective sample size: 28 failed hosted model calls are logged and 56 episodes failed overall; raw failure traces are archived for audit. These are verifiable facts; their exact per‑file SHA‑256s appear in execution/execution_manifest.json. Why the run does not support ensemble claims. Because the consensus stage was not executed, the preregistered hypothesis about the combined defense (validator + 3‑model consensus + human gate) remains untested by these artifacts. We therefore remove ensemble assertions from confirmatory conclusions and recommend a rerun that (A) executes the preregistered ensemble deterministically (seeded per‑model draws archived) and (B) improves orchestration robustness so the planned N completes. Threats to validity. Internal: prompt sensitivity, single shared generation per paired episode (the planned independent multi‑draw ensemble was not run), and provider call failures that generated missing pairs. Construct: the deterministic simulator and validator formalize operational safety but omit hardware timing, partial transient failures, and complex dynamic traffic interactions. External: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic tasks, and simulator environment limit generalization. Conclusion validity: the small absolute differences and low discordant counts limit statistical power for small effects; the preregistered conservative sensitivity bounds results when failed episodes are counted as unsafe. Operational recommendations. For productionization and robust measurement: (i) make consensus draws deterministic and archive per‑draw traces; (ii) harden orchestration to avoid provider‑call failures (see execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl for failure traces and timestamps); (iii) enlarge planned N to offset failed calls; (iv) test validators against device hardware or richer emulators to close construct gaps. Reproducibility and audit. All artifacts required to reproduce the analysis are archived and checksummed (execution/execution_manifest.json lists per‑file SHA‑256); the minimal reproduction set and their checksums are listed in the manuscript evidence bundle. Independent auditors can rederive every reported statistic from the archived scoring JSONs and the analysis CSVs.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired measurement of LLM→action safety and archived full execution provenance. On 272 analyzable pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272 (absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0000,0.0110294]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation prevented testing the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls recorded) reduced effective N. We therefore release the full artifact bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json lists SHA‑256s for every per‑episode file) to support re‑execution and further controlled measurement. Future work should rerun the preregistered ensemble with improved orchestration and larger planned N to measure ensemble effects and to examine robustness across benign/ambiguous/adversarial slices.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).
- Declared hosted model used in execution artifacts: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini").
- Orchestration/adapter used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Deterministic validator used for scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (execution/scoring/*.json include validator_id = "deterministic_netops_validator_v5").
- Exact initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. This archived path+SHA‑256 is the canonical disclosure of the initial master prompt used in the autonomous run.
- Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design with a guarded defense consisting of deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate.
- Verified execution deviation: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage was not executed in this run; audit evidence is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json (stage_counts and condition_counts) and in the provider_call audit (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28). The guarded condition archived corresponds to the deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation. This deviation is artifact‑grounded and reported throughout the manuscript.
- Tools and capabilities permitted and used: deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), hosted LLM provider (declared gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and an isolated deterministic simulator used by the validator. Per‑call provider traces and validator traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/scoring/*.json; their SHA‑256s are listed in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Preregistration freeze and autonomy boundary: The preregistration was locked before observation (SHA‑256 above). After the autonomy lock the system autonomously generated tasks, executed model calls, validated configurations, scored outcomes, analyzed results, and drafted the manuscript; per‑step artifacts and hashes are archived. No human manual editing of technical content, numeric results, validator traces, figures, captions, references, or the Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock.
- Failures and deviations: provider‑call reliability issues produced 28 failed hosted model calls and 56 failed episodes; raw traces and execution logs documenting these failures are archived at execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*.json (see execution/execution_manifest.json for exact file paths and SHA‑256 values). The manuscript reports a preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe; all handling rules and deviations are archived. 
- Human role: The human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock. After the lock all research formulation, execution, analysis, and manuscript text were generated autonomously; provenance artifacts above document the autonomy boundary.
- Reproducibility pointers: execution/execution_manifest.json (full execution accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/responses/*.txt (raw responses), analysis/*.csv (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv), execution/model_configuration.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt (master prompt reference SHA‑256 above) are the key artifact locations to reproduce numbers and audit the run.
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini) — results do not generalize across models or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

The preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run (verified in execution/execution_manifest.json); the guarded condition therefore evaluates validator + simulated human gate on a single generation; ensemble effects are untested.

Missingness: 28 failed hosted model calls and 56 failed episodes reduced effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects. Detailed failure traces are archived for audit (execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*.json).
